newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek gains despite EMU, Bonn worries.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek gains despite EMU, Bonn worries.

text.p: German shares sought on Tuesday to find strength from the firmer dollar and keep up modest gains despite ongoing market jitters about the future of European monetary union.

The 30-share DAX closed bourse trade down 2.42 points at 3,665.01 points, having dipped as low as low as 3,648.45 early in the session. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day trade, was up 2.55 points at 3,671.16 points in post-bourse dealings.
Worries about EMU and the future of Bonn's ruling group, still in the grips of a dispute about how to plug Germany's gaping deficit hole, has sparked bouts of sellings this week.
"The dollar came to the rescue," said a Frankfurt trader.
"But the environment is not the best at the moment. People won't buy into an uncertain market," he added.
The dollar steadied after a period of fluctuation against the mark, trading around 1.71 marks through the day.

Dollar volatility always unsettles the German share market, since so many top German corporates -- notably carmakers, engineering and chemical firms -- depend on the U.S. export market for large amounts of their sales.
Dollar-sensitive car shares such as Volkswagen and BMW both stabilised after Monday's losses.
VW ended bourse trade up seven marks at 1,193 marks and BMW up seven marks at 1,373.
On a day of thin trading, telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom stood out as relatively healthy as traders noted it had passed a technical resistance level at 40.50 marks.
Telekom share ended the bourse up 95 pfennigs at 41 marks.
But traders said the outlook was uncertain with much likely to depend on how other markets finally interpret the worrying signals from France on monetary union.
Dealings will also be influenced by the U.S. market, where overnight Wall Street gains underpinned the DAX on Tuesday.
